problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(1.5,{\sigma }^{2})$ and $P(X<2)=0.5910,$ use the table value to find ${\sigma }^{2},$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5478\,$ | $\,0.5517\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5871\,$ | $\,0.5910\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ | $\,0.6293\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ |

${\sigma }^{2}≈$
{{field-1}}

activity_context.topic_title: Mean and Variance of the Normal Distribution

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-2)=0.7257\,⇒\,P(X\le -2)=0.7257\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le -2) & =0.7257 \\ P(Z\le \frac{-2+3.5}{\sigma }) & =0.7257 \\ Φ(\frac{1.5}{\sigma }) & =0.7257 \\ \frac{1.5}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7257)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.60)=0.7257\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7257)=0.60.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1.5}{\sigma } & =0.60 \\ \sigma  & =2.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}={2.5}^{2}=6.25.\end{aligned}
$$
